A worked example: from SAFs to survival curves

Source: vignettes/articles/walkthrough.Rmd
walkthrough.Rmd

This article takes one analysis from start to finish: load a transplant file, choose a cohort and record every exclusion, add death and graft failure outcomes, check them, draw Kaplan-Meier curves and fit a Cox model. Each step uses the sRtr function that handles it and links the guide that explains it in depth.

The data are made up: 80 kidney transplants and their yearly follow-up forms, written as .sas7bdat files in a temporary folder so that every line runs on this site exactly as it would on your SAFs. The code that makes them is at the end. Every number below comes from those made-up files and says nothing about real transplants.

Point sRtr at your SAFs

Tell sRtr where your SAF folder is, once per session. Keep that folder where your data use agreement and security plan say, outside any project folder tracked by git (Data protection and security).

library(sRtr)
library(dplyr)

set_srtr_wd("path/to/your/SAFs")

On this page, sRtr reads the made-up folder instead. Nothing else in the code changes.

Load the transplant file

load_srtr_file() reads a file by its name in the data dictionary, here TX_KI for kidney transplants. A real TX_KI file has several hundred columns, so name the ones you need with col_select: loading is much faster, and you write down what the analysis uses.

tx <- load_srtr_file(
  "TX_KI",
  col_select = c(
    TRR_ID, PERS_ID, REC_TX_DT, REC_AGE_AT_TX, DON_TY, REC_TX_ORG_TY,
    CAN_PREV_TX, REC_POSTX_LOS, REC_DISCHRG_DT, REC_ACUTE_REJ_EPISODE,
    PERS_OPTN_DEATH_DT, PERS_SSA_DEATH_DT, TFL_DEATH_DT, TFL_GRAFT_DT,
    TFL_LAFUDATE, TFL_ENDTXFU, PERS_RETX
  )
)

The last eight columns are the ones add_time_to_event_outcomes() needs later: transplant admission, death from each source, graft failure, last follow-up, the end of death ascertainment (TFL_ENDTXFU) and retransplant. Coded columns arrive as factors labelled from the dictionary, and dates as dates:

levels(droplevels(tx$REC_TX_ORG_TY))
#> [1] "KI: Kidney"          "KI LI: Kidney-Liver"
class(tx$REC_TX_DT)
#> [1] "Date"

Getting started covers loading in more detail, and Releases, the data dictionary and warnings explains the warnings you may see on your own files.

Count people and transplants

A transplant file has one row per transplant registration (TRR_ID), not one per person (PERS_ID). Someone transplanted twice has two rows. Say which you are counting.

tx |>
  summarise(
    registrations = n_distinct(TRR_ID),
    people = n_distinct(PERS_ID)
  )
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   registrations people
#>           <int>  <int>
#> 1            80     78

Two made-up people have a second transplant here. Files, keys and joins lists the identifier for each unit and shows how to check a join before trusting it.

Choose the cohort, and record every exclusion

This example uses one teaching cohort for both models: each recipient’s first transplant, of a kidney alone. It is close to, but not the same as, the cohorts of SRTR’s program-specific reports (SRTR Technical Methods, section C):

  • their kidney patient survival analyses need a first kidney transplant, so an earlier transplant of another organ does not exclude anyone. Check that the prior-transplant column counts kidney transplants before using it to match them;
  • their graft survival analyses keep repeat transplants of the same organ.

A real analysis builds the cohort each outcome needs.

In the code below, each step keeps a count, and a criterion whose value is missing gets its own step, so a reader can tell exclusion from missing data (Building cohorts draws these steps as a flow diagram).

prev_known <- filter(tx, !is.na(CAN_PREV_TX))
first_tx <- filter(prev_known, CAN_PREV_TX == 0)
organ_known <- filter(first_tx, !is.na(REC_TX_ORG_TY))
cohort <- filter(organ_known, REC_TX_ORG_TY == "KI: Kidney")

tibble(
  step = c(
    "All kidney transplant registrations", "Previous transplants known",
    "First transplant", "Organ type known", "Kidney alone"
  ),
  registrations = c(
    nrow(tx), nrow(prev_known), nrow(first_tx), nrow(organ_known), nrow(cohort)
  ),
  excluded = c(NA, -diff(registrations))
)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 3
#>   step                                registrations excluded
#>   <chr>                                       <int>    <int>
#> 1 All kidney transplant registrations            80       NA
#> 2 Previous transplants known                     80        0
#> 3 First transplant                               78        2
#> 4 Organ type known                               78        0
#> 5 Kidney alone                                   77        1

CAN_PREV_TX and REC_TX_ORG_TY are this example’s way of writing the criteria. On your release, check what each column records in the data dictionary (srtr_dictionary()) before you rely on it: for instance, whether CAN_PREV_TX counts earlier transplants of every organ or of the kidney only.

Add the outcomes

add_time_to_event_outcomes() adds, for each registration, an event indicator (_BINARY), the date follow-up ended (_CENSOR) and the time from transplant in days (_days) for death, two graft failure outcomes, first malignancy and first rejection. It reads the matching follow-up file, here TXF_KI, for the cohort’s registrations only.

out <- add_time_to_event_outcomes(cohort)

Its defaults follow the methods of SRTR’s program-specific reports:

  • Death (REC_DEATH_DT_COMPOSITE) comes from any source (OPTN, Social Security, transplant follow-up), and follow-up ends at TFL_ENDTXFU, the last date to which SRTR ascertains deaths. A recipient with no death in any source is assumed alive to that date.
  • All-cause graft failure (GRAFT_FAIL_ALL_CAUSE_DT) counts graft failure, retransplant or death, whichever comes first, up to the graft’s last follow-up date. _SOURCE says which ended the graft.
  • Death-censored graft failure (TFL_GRAFT_DT) counts only graft failure, and treats death with a working graft as the end of follow-up.

These defaults are provisional and are being evaluated (#300). Each has an argument if your question needs another rule; Follow-up windows and death explains them.

Check the outcomes before modelling

Look at the outcomes as counts before fitting anything. What ended each graft?

out |>
  count(GRAFT_FAIL_ALL_CAUSE_DT_BINARY, GRAFT_FAIL_ALL_CAUSE_DT_SOURCE)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 3
#>   GRAFT_FAIL_ALL_CAUSE_DT_BINARY GRAFT_FAIL_ALL_CAUSE_DT_SOURCE     n
#>                            <int> <chr>                          <int>
#> 1                              0 death                              4
#> 2                              0 NA                                43
#> 3                              1 death                             17
#> 4                              1 graft_failure                     13

A row with a date in GRAFT_FAIL_ALL_CAUSE_DT and _BINARY of 0 had its first event after the graft’s last follow-up, so it is not counted. Any missing time drops out of the models below; count them:

out |>
  summarise(
    death_time_missing = sum(is.na(REC_DEATH_DT_COMPOSITE_days)),
    graft_time_missing = sum(is.na(GRAFT_FAIL_ALL_CAUSE_DT_days))
  )
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   death_time_missing graft_time_missing
#>                <int>              <int>
#> 1                  0                  0

The death window matters. Some made-up deaths are known only from Social Security records, after the recipient’s last follow-up form. The default counts them; ending follow-up at the last form instead (death_window = "follow_up") does not:

follow_up <- add_time_to_event_outcomes(cohort, death_window = "follow_up")
c(
  deaths_to_TFL_ENDTXFU = sum(out$REC_DEATH_DT_COMPOSITE_BINARY, na.rm = TRUE),
  deaths_to_last_form = sum(follow_up$REC_DEATH_DT_COMPOSITE_BINARY, na.rm = TRUE)
)
#> deaths_to_TFL_ENDTXFU   deaths_to_last_form 
#>                    23                    19

The follow-up forms read are summarized in the txf_report attribute:

report <- attr(out, "txf_report")
report[c("follow_up_file", "registrations", "registrations_with_forms", "forms")]
#> $follow_up_file
#> [1] "TXF_KI"
#> 
#> $registrations
#> [1] 77
#> 
#> $registrations_with_forms
#> [1] 64
#> 
#> $forms
#> [1] 311

On your own files, every count you share outside your secure environment must follow your agreement: aggregate counts only, with small counts masked (Share counts only).

Kaplan-Meier curves

The survival package fits the models. Convert days to years for the plot.

library(survival)

out <- out |>
  mutate(
    death_years = REC_DEATH_DT_COMPOSITE_days / 365.25,
    graft_years = GRAFT_FAIL_ALL_CAUSE_DT_days / 365.25,
    donor = factor(DON_TY, levels = c("C", "L"), labels = c("Deceased", "Living"))
  )

km <- survfit(Surv(death_years, REC_DEATH_DT_COMPOSITE_BINARY) ~ donor, data = out)

plot(
  km,
  lty = c(1, 2),
  xlab = "Years after transplant",
  ylab = "Patient survival",
  main = "Made-up data"
)
legend("bottomleft", legend = c("Deceased donor", "Living donor"), lty = c(1, 2), bty = "n")

Survival at one, three and five years, with the number still at risk:

summary(km, times = c(1, 3, 5))
#> Call: survfit(formula = Surv(death_years, REC_DEATH_DT_COMPOSITE_BINARY) ~ 
#>     donor, data = out)
#> 
#>                 donor=Deceased 
#>  time n.risk n.event survival std.err lower 95% CI upper 95% CI
#>     1     45       5    0.900  0.0424        0.821        0.987
#>     3     38       7    0.760  0.0604        0.650        0.888
#>     5     29       4    0.675  0.0669        0.556        0.820
#> 
#>                 donor=Living 
#>  time n.risk n.event survival std.err lower 95% CI upper 95% CI
#>     1     27       0    1.000  0.0000        1.000        1.000
#>     3     24       3    0.889  0.0605        0.778        1.000
#>     5     20       1    0.848  0.0699        0.722        0.997

A Cox model

All-cause graft failure by donor type, adjusted for age at transplant, in the same teaching cohort (first transplants only; SRTR’s graft survival analyses would also include repeat kidney transplants):

cox <- coxph(
  Surv(graft_years, GRAFT_FAIL_ALL_CAUSE_DT_BINARY) ~ donor + REC_AGE_AT_TX,
  data = out
)
summary(cox)$conf.int
#>               exp(coef) exp(-coef) lower .95 upper .95
#> donorLiving   0.7214388  1.3861190 0.3290273  1.581857
#> REC_AGE_AT_TX 1.0400259  0.9615146 1.0138421  1.066886

With 80 made-up transplants the estimates are imprecise and mean nothing. On real data, check proportional hazards (cox.zph()) and think about competing risks before you interpret a graft failure model (Follow-up windows and death).

Describing the methods

A methods section should let a reader rebuild the cohort and the outcomes. For the analysis above it would say, at least:

  • the SAF release and file (TX_KI), and the cohort criteria with the number excluded at each step;
  • the unit of analysis: transplant registrations, not people;
  • that deaths came from OPTN, Social Security and transplant follow-up records, and that follow-up for death ended at SRTR’s cohort date (TFL_ENDTXFU), with recipients not reported dead assumed alive;
  • that graft failure was all-cause (graft failure, retransplant or death), censored at the last follow-up date, as in SRTR’s program-specific reports (SRTR Technical Methods);
  • the sRtr version used (packageVersion("sRtr")).

On your own files

Replace the made-up folder with your own by calling set_srtr_wd(); the rest of the code is the same. Then:

  • run the checks in Checking sRtr on your own SAFs once for your release;
  • read the warnings: a column that is missing, or a code the dictionary does not list, changes what a step does;
  • for kidney-pancreas (TX_KP), each graft has its own outcome columns (_KI and _PA).

The made-up files

The code that wrote the two made-up files used above. Every value is invented; the column names come from the data dictionary.

library(dplyr)

safs <- file.path(tempdir(), "made-up-safs")
dir.create(safs, showWarnings = FALSE)
set.seed(2026)
n <- 80
tx_date <- as.Date("2014-01-01") + sample(0:1825, n, replace = TRUE)
end_date <- as.Date("2022-12-31")
older <- sample(c(FALSE, TRUE), n, replace = TRUE)
living <- runif(n) < 0.3

# Death, graft failure and loss to follow-up at made-up rates.
death <- tx_date + round(365.25 * rexp(n, 0.04 * ifelse(older, 2.2, 1) * ifelse(living, 0.6, 1)))
graft <- tx_date + round(365.25 * rexp(n, 0.05))
lost <- tx_date + round(365.25 * rexp(n, 0.04))
last_fu <- pmin(death, lost, end_date)
reported <- death <= last_fu
ssa_only <- death > last_fu & death <= end_date

made_up_tx <- tibble(
  TRR_ID = 900000 + seq_len(n),
  PERS_ID = 800000 + c(seq_len(n - 2), 1, 2),
  REC_TX_DT = tx_date,
  REC_AGE_AT_TX = ifelse(older, sample(60:75, n, TRUE), sample(20:59, n, TRUE)),
  DON_TY = ifelse(living, "L", "C"),
  REC_TX_ORG_TY = c(rep("KI", n - 3), "KI LI", "KI", "KI"),
  CAN_PREV_TX = c(rep(0, n - 2), 1, 1),
  REC_POSTX_LOS = sample(3:10, n, replace = TRUE),
  REC_DISCHRG_DT = tx_date + 7,
  REC_ACUTE_REJ_EPISODE = sample(c(1, 3), n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.1, 0.9)),
  PERS_OPTN_DEATH_DT = if_else(reported, death, as.Date(NA_character_)),
  PERS_SSA_DEATH_DT = if_else(ssa_only, death, as.Date(NA_character_)),
  TFL_DEATH_DT = if_else(reported, death, as.Date(NA_character_)),
  TFL_GRAFT_DT = if_else(graft <= last_fu, graft, as.Date(NA_character_)),
  TFL_LAFUDATE = last_fu,
  TFL_ENDTXFU = end_date,
  PERS_RETX = as.Date(NA)
)

# One follow-up form a year until last follow-up.
made_up_forms <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
  years <- seq_len(floor(as.numeric(last_fu[i] - tx_date[i]) / 365.25))
  if (length(years) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  tibble(
    TRR_ID = made_up_tx$TRR_ID[i],
    TRR_FOL_ID = made_up_tx$TRR_ID[i] * 100 + years,
    ORG_TY = "KI",
    TFL_PX_STAT_DT = tx_date[i] + round(365.25 * years),
    TFL_FOL_CD = 10 * years,
    TFL_MALIG = sample(c("N", "Y"), length(years), TRUE, c(0.95, 0.05)),
    TFL_ACUTE_REJ_EPISODE = sample(c(3, 1), length(years), TRUE, c(0.93, 0.07))
  )
}))

haven::write_sas(made_up_tx, file.path(safs, "TX_KI.sas7bdat"))
haven::write_sas(made_up_forms, file.path(safs, "TXF_KI.sas7bdat"))

# Point sRtr at the made-up folder for this page only; restored at the end.
old_wd <- Sys.getenv("SRTR_WD", unset = NA)
Sys.setenv(SRTR_WD = safs)

References

Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients. Technical methods for the program-specific reports. https://srtr.hrsa.gov/transplant-professionals/program-specific-report/technical-methods-for-the-program-specific-reports/ (accessed 20 November 2026).
